channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Trump and Iran cannot agree on what they just signed
item.description: The 60-day framework that Trump and Iran's president signed at Versailles on June 17 was meant to wind the war down and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. A week on, the two capitals cannot agree on what the document actually says.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar surges near recent highs as markets watch PCE inflation and Middle East
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) traded near the 101.00 level on a positive note on Monday, near the 13-month high of 101.13 reached on Friday, as investors balanced softer Oil prices, renewed hopes for peace between the United States (US) and Iran, and expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could remain re

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens vs Dollar, Euro as SNB gets relief
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) loses ground against the US Dollar (USD) and the Euro (EUR) on Monday as risk appetite improves amid the start of US-Iran talks, which US Vice President JD Vance deemed positive.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Stays pressured against US Dollar as trades cautiously – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that Malaysian Ringgit (MYR) has softened despite supportive domestic data, as Fed-led hawkish repricing keeps US Treasury yields and the US Dollar (USD) firm. Softer Oil offers only a buffer rather than a catalyst.

item.title: United States Dollar Index rises, remains supported near 101.00
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the Greenback against a basket of major currencies, is trading near the 101.00 area on Monday, up 0.26% on the day at the time of writing.

item.title: Mexican Peso weakens as Fed repricing lifts US Dollar ahead of Banxico
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) posts a 0.34% loss on Monday as the Greenback recovers some ground, driven by the Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish tilt, which pushed the US Dollar (USD) higher. At the time of writing, USD/MXN trades at 17.35 after bouncing off daily lows of 17.30.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Bears defend 50-day SMA as intervention risks linger
item.description: AUD/JPY extends its sideways price action on Monday near levels last seen in September 1990, as persistent weakness in the Japanese Yen (JPY) keeps the cross supported while fears of another intervention by Japanese authorities limit further gains.

item.title: Chinese Yuan : Testing 6.8000 within broader range against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that USD/CNH spiked to 6.7980 before reversing, leaving the pair broadly unchanged near 6.78.

item.title: For the Canadian Dollar, the trade war beats the data
item.description: A hot inflation print and a rebound in Crude Oil ought to be a recipe for a stronger commodity currency, which makes the Canadian Dollar's slide to fresh 14-month lows all the more telling.

item.title: The Japanese Yen makes British political chaos look orderly
item.description: There is something faintly absurd about a currency pair holding this high while one half of it represents a country that has just lost its prime minister. GBP/JPY settled Monday close to 214.00, sitting on its rising 50-day average after a pullback from this month's peak near 216.50.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Pressured against US Dollar as MAS tightening eyed – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that USD/SGD is trading with a bid tone on a firmer US Dollar (USD) backdrop, with resistance around 1.2940 and support near 1.2840/50.

item.title: Gold price rises as Iran talks knock Oil lower
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price posts modest gains of 0.50% on Monday as talks between the US and Iran began on a positive note, driving Oil prices lower and reducing inflation expectations. At the time of writing, the XAU/USD pair trades at $4,179, after bouncing off daily lows of $4,136.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar falls as hawkish Fed, fragile US-Iran truce boost the US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD trades in negative territory around 0.5730 on Monday, extending its retreat for the fourth consecutive day. The pair hit its lowest level since April 8, against a backdrop of broad US Dollar (USD) strength and persistent uncertainty surrounding the US-Iran peace process.

item.title: Malaysia: Price pressures and policy hold – UOB
item.description: UOB economists Julia Goh and Loke Siew Ting note Malaysia’s May headline inflation rose to 2.0% year-on-year, the highest since July 2024, driven by Food, Housing, Utilities and Transport. Year-to-date inflation of 1.7% supports their full-year 2.0% forecast.

item.title: Asia FX: Growth support versus Fed risks – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan notes that Asian currencies should benefit from stronger regional growth differentials versus the US, particularly in AI-related export economies such as South Korea, Taiwan, Malaysia and Singapore.

item.title: Australian Dollar falls near 0.7000 ahead of US PCE inflation data
item.description: The AUD/USD pair fell near the 0.700 area on Monday, struggling to extend gains as investors remain cautious ahead of the upcoming US Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index (PCE), the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) preferred inflation gauge.

item.title: Euro languishes near three-month lows against US Dollar despite progress in US-Iran talks
item.description: EUR/USD trades under pressure on Monday, extending losses from the previous week as expectations of a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) underpin the US Dollar (USD), even as easing tensions in the Middle East curb safe-haven demand for the Greenback.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average is green for all the wrong reasons
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) booked a green close on Monday, adding roughly 167 points, or 0.3%, on a session that was anything but bullish underneath.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range trade against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD remains supported around 1.29 as the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (S$NEER) trades near the top of its band, implying the pair should hover close to this level.

item.title: British Pound rises as US-Iran talks offset UK political shock
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) advances some 0.14% on Monday as US-Iran negotiations laid a “good foundation,” according to US Vice President JD Vance, after ending the first round of talks in Switzerland.

item.title: Carry trade: Recovery prospects build – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that iFlow Carry has turned negatively significant for the first time in 2026, signalling ongoing unwinding of carry trades but also a potential contrarian opportunity.

item.title: Japanese Yen retreats from highs, trends toward 161.00
item.description: The USD/JPY pair sank as low as 161.07 on Monday, retreating from highs near 161.90 as traders remain alert to possible Japanese intervention after the pair moved close to a four-decade high.

item.title: British Pound: Political risks and BoE path shape outlook – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s Dominic Bunning highlights that British Pound (GBP) has reacted calmly to Keir Starmer’s resignation, with investors focusing on the prospect of Andy Burnham becoming Prime Minister and his choice of Chancellor.

item.title: Silver price rises on US-Iran diplomatic progress, upside capped by hawkish Fed
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $65.90 at the time of writing on Monday, up 1.69% on the day and snapping a three-day losing streak. The white metal is attracting renewed investor interest as markets assess the implications of diplomatic progress between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC patience guided by contained core – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Matthieu Arseneau and Alexandra Ducharme note that Canadian headline inflation rose to 3.2% in May, above the Bank of Canada’s (BoC) target range, driven mainly by higher gasoline and food prices.

item.title: Fed: Hawkish hold extends through 2027 – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities, led by Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir, reports that the Federal Reserve (Fed) has shifted hawkishly and is expected to keep policy rates on hold through 2026 and 2027.

item.title: British Pound: Focus shifts to leadership and fiscal risks – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Shreyas Gopal notes that markets had largely anticipated Andy Burnham becoming UK Prime Minister by the Autumn Budget, leaving the risk premium in Sterling broadly unchanged.

item.title: Gold climbs as US-Iran talks make progress, Fed rate hike bets cap upside
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges higher on Monday as traders react to signs of progress in US-Iran negotiations following the first round of direct talks held earlier in the day in Switzerland, with Pakistan and Qatar acting as mediators.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Inflation driven by energy – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Abbey Xu notes that Canadian inflation rose to 3.2% year-over-year in May, mainly due to higher energy prices, airfares and food costs.

item.title: Canadian Dollar struggles to gain traction despite stronger inflation data
item.description: USD/CAD trades little changed on Monday after a brief bout of weakness following stronger-than-expected Canadian inflation data. At the time of writing, the pair is trading around 1.4165, hovering near its highest level since April 2025.
